text: What is the primary cause of depreciation of assets?
explanation: Depreciation is caused by various factors including wear and tear, efflux of time, and obsolescence. As per the NCERT textbook, these factors contribute to the decrease in the value of assets over their useful life.
subject: Accountancy

text: Which method of depreciation is based on the assumption that the asset will lose its value evenly over its useful life?
explanation: The Straight Line Method (SLM) of depreciation assumes that the asset will lose its value evenly over its useful life. This method calculates depreciation as $\frac{Cost - Residual\ Value}{Useful\ Life}$, as explained in the NCERT textbook.
subject: Accountancy

text: What is the formula to calculate the depreciation under the Written Down Value (WDV) Method?
options: $Depreciation = \frac{Opening\ Balance - Residual\ Value}{Useful\ Life} \times Rate\ of\ Depreciation$
explanation: The Written Down Value (WDV) Method calculates depreciation as $Rate\ of\ Depreciation \times Opening\ Balance$. This method takes into account the reducing balance of the asset over its useful life, as explained in the NCERT textbook.
subject: Accountancy

text: What is the main difference between provisions and reserves?
options: Provisions are made for known liabilities, while reserves are made for unknown liabilities
Provisions are made for unknown liabilities, while reserves are made for known liabilities
Provisions are made for revenue items, while reserves are made for capital items
Provisions are made for capital items, while reserves are made for revenue items
correctAnswer: Provisions are made for known liabilities, while reserves are made for unknown liabilities
explanation: Provisions are made for known liabilities, such as depreciation, bad debts, etc. On the other hand, reserves are made for unknown liabilities or for strengthening the financial position of the business, as explained in the NCERT textbook.
subject: Accountancy

text: Which of the following is a type of reserve?
explanation: A general reserve is a type of reserve that is created by transferring a portion of the profits to a reserve account. It is not a provision, but a reserve, as explained in the NCERT textbook.
subject: Accountancy

text: What is the purpose of creating a reserve?
options: To strengthen the financial position of the business
correctAnswer: To strengthen the financial position of the business
explanation: The purpose of creating a reserve is to strengthen the financial position of the business by setting aside a portion of the profits. This helps to meet unknown liabilities, contingencies, or future expenses, as explained in the NCERT textbook.
subject: Accountancy

text: Which of the following is a capital reserve?
explanation: A share premium reserve is a type of capital reserve that is created when the company issues shares at a premium. It is a capital reserve because it is created from the proceeds of the issue of shares, as explained in the NCERT textbook.
subject: Accountancy

text: What is the effect of depreciation on the financial statements?
options: It has no effect on the net profit
explanation: Depreciation is a non-cash expense that reduces the net profit of the business. It is charged to the profit and loss account, which reduces the net profit, as explained in the NCERT textbook.
subject: Accountancy

text: Which of the following is a revenue reserve?
explanation: A dividend equalization reserve is a type of revenue reserve that is created to stabilize the dividend payout. It is a revenue reserve because it is created from the revenue profits of the business, as explained in the NCERT textbook.
subject: Accountancy

text: What is the purpose of creating a provision for bad debts?
options: To meet the known liability of bad debts
To strengthen the financial position of the business
correctAnswer: To meet the known liability of bad debts
explanation: The purpose of creating a provision for bad debts is to meet the known liability of bad debts. It is a provision because it is made for a known liability, as explained in the NCERT textbook.
subject: Accountancy

text: Which of the following is not a type of provision?
explanation: A general reserve is not a provision, but a reserve. Provisions are made for known liabilities, while reserves are made for unknown liabilities or for strengthening the financial position of the business, as explained in the NCERT textbook.
